hero.lede: A Rust L1 with BFT finality, hybrid post-quantum signatures and an EAVM surface for EVM wallets. Read the chain with a curl; sign your first transaction with the SDK.

hub.pathsLede: Each solves a different problem. You are not picking forever — the node and the SDK talk to the same API you can already call today.
hub.path1Desc: Nothing to install. The public API answers JSON on every read endpoint: state, blocks, accounts, tokens, validators.
hub.path2Desc: The Rust SDK builds the canonical envelope, signs locally with secp256k1 + ML-DSA-44 and submits it. No consensus rule reimplemented.
hub.path3Desc: eav7-core syncs, validates and — with enough stake — produces blocks. Listener at home, validator on a VPS.
hub.firstCallTitle: Sixty seconds to your first JSON
hub.firstCallBody1: Every read is plain HTTP, no key and no special header. /status returns the current height, the finalized height, the chain head and the active validator set.
hub.firstCallBody2: Monetary values come back as integer strings in e7 — the smallest unit of the coin. Reading a balance is reading an integer; formatting is your presentation layer's problem.
hub.surfacesLede: The same chain serves three audiences: HTTP integrators, EVM wallets and consensus participants.
hub.restDesc: Native-scheme reads and writes, in JSON. The surface the explorer and the SDK use.
hub.eavmDesc: Compatible with MetaMask, Trust Wallet and EVM tooling. Chain ID 72020.
hub.p2pDesc: Block and transaction gossip between nodes. How the Core syncs.
hub.unitsBody: 1 EAV7 = 1,000,000 e7 on the HTTP API (CHAIN.UNIT). On the EAVM surface wallets assume 18 decimals, so each e7 is 10¹² wei (CHAIN.EAVM_WEI_PER_E7). Mixing the two scales is the most expensive integration mistake.
hub.ctaTitle: The network is up. Your code is the missing part.
hub.ctaLede: Start with a read, finish with a transaction confirmed in a block.
hub.path4Desc: Step-by-step guides for the tasks that actually come up: sign and broadcast, transfer, issue a token, prove a balance.
hub.path5Desc: Address, hybrid key, nonce, energy, finality. Four concept pages that head off most integration mistakes.

quickstart.title: From first curl to first transaction
quickstart.lede: Five steps: pick a target, read the state, read an account, run your own node if you want one, and sign a transfer.
quickstart.step1Intro: Everything here works against any node on the mesh. Start with the public one and swap the URL once yours is up.
quickstart.targetPublicNote: Open reads, no key. Same node that serves the explorer.
quickstart.targetLocalNote: What eav7-core exposes after `run`. Port is set at init time.
quickstart.targetEavmNote: For EVM tooling only. Not the native HTTP API.
quickstart.step2Intro: /status is the handshake: if it answers, the rest of the API answers.
quickstart.step2CalloutBody: At the root (/) the node returns the JSON API index when the header is present — without it, the root is the explorer's HTML page. Every other endpoint always answers JSON.
quickstart.step3Intro: The same endpoint takes a native address (E7…) and an EAVM address (0x…): both point at the same account.
quickstart.step3CalloutBody: nonce is what already landed in a block. nextNonce also accounts for the mempool — it is what stops two transactions from fighting over the same number.
quickstart.step4Intro: In listen mode the Core only syncs and serves the API. That is enough to develop against real data without depending on somebody else's node.
quickstart.step4Body: Modes, candidacy, default paths and service installation live in
quickstart.step5Intro: Writing is always a signed transaction. The SDK builds the canonical payload, signs locally and POSTs to /tx — no private key ever leaves your machine.
quickstart.step5CalloutBody: amount is an integer in e7, not in EAV7. Sending 5 EAV7 means sending 5,000,000. Get the scale wrong and you send a millionth — or a million times too much.
quickstart.step5FeeTitle: fee is a limit, not a price
quickstart.step5FeeBody: The fee field authorizes a burn ceiling. The actual burn comes from the resource model (energy + bandwidth) and is not paid to the block producer.
quickstart.pathsTitle: Pick what you want to do first
quickstart.pathsIntro: All three entry points use the same chain and the same API. What differs is what you need in hand before you start.
quickstart.pathReadBody: A curl is enough. State, blocks, accounts, tokens and validators answer JSON with no key and no special header. Start with the next section.
quickstart.pathWriteTitle: Sign and send — Rust SDK and a wallet
quickstart.pathWriteBody: eav7-sdk builds the canonical envelope, signs it with secp256k1 + ML-DSA-44 and submits. You need a wallet file and a balance for the fee.
quickstart.pathNodeBody: The node syncs, validates and, with enough stake, produces blocks. A listener is up in minutes; standing for election needs 1,000 EAV7 staked.

api.title: HTTP API
api.lede: The node's public surface. Every response is JSON, every read is open, and every monetary value is an integer string in e7.
api.surfacesIntro: Examples use the public node; swap the host for yours and everything else is identical.
api.specRestNote: Port 6070 when the node runs locally.
api.specEavmNote: Port 7070 when the node runs locally. JSON-RPC only.
api.specFormatNote: Required at the root to get the JSON index instead of HTML.
api.specAuthValue: None for reads or for POST /tx
api.specAuthNote: Only admin endpoints require a token.
api.unitsIntro: Two scales share one ledger. Knowing which one you are in is half the integration.
api.unitUnitNote: The scale of the HTTP API and of consensus. Values are strings because they exceed 2⁶⁴.
api.unitWeiNote: Used only on the EAVM surface, where wallets assume 18 decimals.
api.unitTypesNote: Parse with BigInt/u128. Floating point loses precision on real balances.
api.unitsCalloutBody: The two constants compose: 10⁶ e7 per EAV7 × 10¹² wei per e7. An EVM wallet showing 18 decimals is right; so is the API showing 6.
api.readIntro: All open, all JSON, all idempotent.
api.pageIntro: Lists take limit; historical feeds page with a before cursor, which is the height of the last item on the previous page.
api.writeIntro: Writing is always a signed envelope. The node validates signature, nonce, resources and type before admitting it to the mempool.
api.writeBody: To build and sign the envelope without reimplementing consensus, use the
api.adminCalloutBody: These require the x-admin-token header carrying EAV7_ADMIN_TOKEN. With the variable unset the endpoints are disabled — it is not an open fallback.
api.internalIntro: Value an EAVM contract moves during execution is not a signed transaction and has no hash of its own. It is indexed separately.
api.internalCalloutBody: A derivable node-local index, like /logs: it never enters the stateRoot. Only successful executions emit — a reverted call leaves no record and the value returns to the sender.

ep.status: Chain state: height, finalized height, head hash, supply, treasury, validators and block reward.
ep.blockByRef: Block by height or hash; includes size, the block line's length in bytes.
ep.chain: Contiguous range of blocks, capped by MAX_CHAIN_PAGE.
ep.stats: Explorer aggregates: accounts, stake, 24h volume, TPS and time series.
ep.address: E7 or 0x account: balance, staked, nonce, nextNonce, energy, feeExempt, isValidator and tokens.
ep.addressTxs: Wallet transactions, newest first, with a before cursor.
ep.addressAnalysis: Account aggregates for charts: counts, sent, received, by type and counterparties.
ep.proof: Merkle proof of the account against the stateRoot — verify a balance without downloading state.
ep.internal: Internal transfers from EAVM execution, in a node-local index.
ep.tx: Transaction by id, confirmed or still in the mempool.
ep.logs: Recent EAVM events, in a node-local ring buffer.
ep.search: Prefix search across addresses, tokens, blocks and transactions.
ep.tokenTransfers: Token transfers, with a before cursor.
ep.name: Resolves an EAV-NS name to its E7 address, or 404.
ep.validators: Active set current + standby bank/bankSize; maxValidators, slotProducer, and performance.
ep.governance: Governable parameters and on-chain governance state.
ep.governanceProposals: Proposals under vote and already decided.
ep.contract: Verification metadata for an EAVM contract, or 404.
ep.bridgeTransfer: A single bridge transfer, by id.
ep.aiTasks: Tasks on the native AI layer.
ep.postTx: Submits a signed transaction in the hybrid scheme.
ep.postVerify: Verifies a contract: the submitted bytecode must match the on-chain code.
ep.postBlock: Receives a block over P2P gossip.

api.taskTitle: I want to do X — what do I call?
api.taskIntro: Nobody opens a reference looking for an endpoint; they open it looking for an answer. This table goes from intent to the exact surface.

read.balance: Get the balance and stake of an account
read.proveBalance: Prove a balance without trusting the node
read.tx: Look up a transaction by id
read.head: Find the head of the chain
read.range: Sweep a block range to index it
read.final: Know how far the chain is irreversible
read.search: Resolve text that could be an address, block or tx

write.verify: Verify a contract's source against its bytecode

assets.tokens: List EAV20 tokens or read one of them
assets.name: Resolve an EAV-NS name to an address

network.validators: See the active set and each validator's performance
network.logs: Read EAVM events and internal transfers

tx.title: Transactions
tx.lede: The eav20 protocol has {n} transaction types, and the list is closed on purpose: a node that accepts a type it cannot execute diverges from state.
tx.envelopeIntro: This is the object POST /tx takes. Fields above the blank line go into the signed payload; the ones below are the result of signing.
tx.fieldProtocol: Scheme constants. Any divergence is an immediate rejection.
tx.fieldAmount: Unsigned decimals in e7, as text — real balances exceed 2⁶⁴.
tx.fieldNonce: Per-account sequence. Use the API's nextNonce, which already counts the mempool.
tx.fieldData: Free payload per transaction type. No floating point: fractions travel as text.
tx.fieldSignature: Hybrid signature: classic secp256k1 plus post-quantum ML-DSA-44.
tx.fieldId: Hash of the signing payload. The id you see in the explorer.
tx.costIntro: EAV7 does not auction block space. Cost comes from a per-account resource model — energy and bandwidth — and the fee field only bounds how much of it you authorize burning.
tx.costCalloutBody: The effective burn is computed by the state machine from the energy and bandwidth consumed. It is not paid to the block producer: it leaves circulation.
tx.forkCalloutBody: Consensus changes are gated by fork height (CHAIN.FORK_HEIGHTS). On a network brought up with EAV7_GENESIS_ACTIVE=1, every type is active from block 0.
tx.catalogIntro: Fee limit in e7, straight from CHAIN.FEES. Filter by name or description.
tx.sendIntro: All land in the same mempool; what changes is who builds and signs the envelope.
tx.sendSdk: Builds, signs and submits in one call. The recommended path.
tx.sendRest: You build and sign; the node only validates and accepts. Requires the canonical payload byte for byte.
tx.sendEavm: EAVM envelope with a raw secp256k1 signature, for EVM tooling.

type.UNSTAKE: Starts unbonding a slice of the stake.
type.EAVM_TRANSFER: Moves value on the EAVM surface, in the 0x world.
type.DELEGATE_RESOURCE: Sponsors energy or bandwidth for another account.
type.META_TX: Executes a transaction sponsored by a third party.
type.TOKEN_APPROVE: Authorizes a spender over your balance.
type.TOKEN_TRANSFER_FROM: Moves balance using a granted allowance.
type.TOKEN_BLACKLIST: Blocks an address on the token.
type.NFT_MINT: Mints an item in the collection.
type.NFT_TRANSFER: Transfers an item to another account.
type.AI_REFUND: Refunds payment for an unanswered task.
type.AI_COMMIT: Commits a result in the commit-reveal quorum.
type.AI_CLAIM: Claims payment inside the challenge window.
type.AI_CHALLENGE: Disputes a result inside the window.
type.AI_VERDICT: Records the verdict of a challenge.
type.AI_AWARD: Awards the task to the winning bid.
type.BRIDGE_OUT: Sends value off-chain through the bridge.
type.BRIDGE_COMMITTEE_UPDATE: Updates the committee that signs the bridge.
type.EAVM_DEPLOY: Deploys a contract on the EAVM.

eavm.title: EAVM
eavm.lede: The surface compatible with the EVM ecosystem. Same chain, same ledger — seen through a wallet that expects 18 decimals and 0x addresses.
eavm.connectIntro: The button uses the canonical wallet_switchEthereumChain → wallet_addEthereumChain flow. For wallets that inject no provider, the parameters alongside cover manual setup.
eavm.paramsIntro: The card above already has the values to copy. These are the traps behind them.
eavm.paramChainId: Decimal when adding the network by hand, hexadecimal over JSON-RPC.
eavm.paramRpc: The public endpoint is rpc.eavscan.com; with the node on your machine it is port 7070.
eavm.paramCurrency: The wallet shows 18 decimals; the native API uses 6. Same amount, different scale.
eavm.rpcIntro: Enough for wallets, contract reads and submitting a signed transaction.

rpc.net_version: Network id in decimal, as a string.
rpc.net_listening: Whether the node is accepting connections.
rpc.eth_accounts: Empty list — the node holds no user keys.
rpc.eth_getTransactionReceipt: Receipt with status, gas and logs.
rpc.eth_getLogs: Events filtered by address and topic.
rpc.eth_call: Runs the call without writing state.

eavm.gapsIntro: Compatibility is deliberately partial. These methods are not served:
eavm.gapsCalloutBody: There is no eth_sendTransaction because the node custodies no keys: sign in the wallet and submit with eth_sendRawTransaction. There is no WebSocket and no subscriptions either — poll /logs or eth_getLogs to follow events.
eavm.unknownBody: Anything outside the list returns JSON-RPC error -32601, not an empty response. Silently swallowing the unknown is how a second, divergent implementation is born.
eavm.valueIntro: From CHAIN.EAVM_VALUE_HEIGHT onward, EAVM contracts are payable over a unified ledger.
eavm.valueLedgerBody: The 0x world balance IS the matching native account. Value flows in, circulates and flows out without getting stuck in a bridge.
eavm.valueInternalBody: Value moved by execution is not a signed transaction and has no hash of its own: it shows up in GET /internal, outside consensus.
eavm.valueUnitsBody: The RPC answers in wei; consensus works in e7. The factor is 10¹² and it holds both ways.

sdk.title: Rust SDK
sdk.lede: eav7-sdk depends on the consensus library and never on the node crate. You sign with the same code the node validates with — no second implementation of the rule.
sdk.installIntro: A Rust crate on edition 2024. The HTTP client is synchronous (ureq): no async runtime is forced on the caller.
sdk.installCalloutBody: If you already have a runtime, call it inside spawn_blocking; if you do not, write a plain script. Key generation (secp256k1 and ML-DSA-44) ships with the SDK.
sdk.clientIntro: Without a wallet the client only reads. With one it builds, signs and submits.
sdk.readIntro: Typed methods return structs; get returns raw JSON for whatever has no type yet.
sdk.proofIntro: A light client does not need the full state to check a balance — a Merkle proof is enough, as long as the root comes from a verified header.
sdk.proofCalloutBody: Passing None to saldo_provado verifies against the root that /proof itself returned, which only proves internal consistency. Fetching the root from the header first is what turns the proof into a guarantee.
sdk.writeIntro: The shortcuts cover the common types; executar builds any of the 58, and montar signs without touching the network.
sdk.senderIntro: Remetente reserves the nonce locally instead of asking the node on every send.
sdk.senderCalloutTitle: Why not use the client directly
sdk.senderCalloutBody: Two consecutive calls read the same nextNonce if the first has not reached the mempool yet — and the second is rejected. Any rejection or network error resyncs the sender.
sdk.examplesIntro: Two runnable examples live in the crate: one reading with proof, one writing.

m.conta: Typed account: balance, stake, next nonce, unbonding and claimable reward.
m.proximo_nonce: Next nonce for the account, mempool-aware.
m.bloco: Block by height, hash or latest.
m.historico: One page of wallet history, with the next cursor.
m.validadores_tipados: Active set joined with each validator's performance.
m.contrato: Verification metadata for an EAVM contract.
m.get: Escape hatch: any API path, raw JSON.
m.raiz_confiavel_do_header: stateRoot taken from a verified header.
m.saldo_provado: Balance checked by Merkle against the given root.
m.transferir: Builds, signs and submits a TRANSFER.
m.reivindicar_recompensa: Claims voter rewards from a validator.
m.executar: Builds and submits any type, with the spec you shape.
m.montar: Signs locally and returns the Tx, without touching the network.
m.aguardar_confirmacao: Blocks until the transaction lands in a block, or the timeout fires.
m.remetente: Opens a sender with local nonce reservation.

core.title: EAV7 Core
core.lede: Anyone can run a node and manage stake and candidacy without reading the monorepo. Phones do not produce blocks: the Core on a PC or VPS verifies and, if you want, produces.
core.buildIntro: eav7-core and eav7-node land in the same directory and are used together.
core.releaseBody: Published by tag or via the release-core workflow: tarball and zip with .sha256 for Linux x64, Linux arm64, macOS arm64 and Windows x64.
core.modesIntro: The mode is stored in the config and decides whether the node just follows or competes to produce.

mode.listen: Syncs and serves the API. No validator wallet: does not produce.
mode.candidate: Wallet attached. Produces if it sits in the top 27 by weight.
mode.validator: Same as candidate; the declared intent is a 24/7 VPS.

core.modesShortcut: Run shortcuts: eav7-core listen | candidate | validator --dir …
core.listenIntro: Three commands and the node is syncing. The right mode for developing against real data.
core.listenBody: In listen mode, point --peers at another node on the mesh. --url redirects the commands to a different API when it is not the port recorded in core.json.
core.candidateIntro: Requires balance in the Core's wallet. Command amounts are in EAV7, not e7.
core.candidateCalloutBody: Below that the candidacy does not enter the election. The elected set is the top 27 by weight — stake plus received votes — and it is re-evaluated every round.
core.pathOverride: Overrides the default directory on any system.
core.keysIntro: The node needs far less than your main wallet. Keep it that way.
core.keyHotNote: Mode 0600 on the server. Only what is needed to sign blocks.
core.keyTreasuryNote: Off the VPS. Never on the same disk as a production Core.
core.keyForceNote: Regenerates the node wallet. Back up first — there is no undo.
core.serviceIntro: Example files live under deploy/ in the repository.
core.serviceCalloutBody: macOS and Windows work fine as a home listener or candidate. For continuous production, prefer a Linux VPS.
core.stackIntro: One command brings up protocol and explorer together.

networks.title: Networks
networks.lede: Where to point the client, which port serves each surface, and the protocol parameters you should not have to discover by trial and error.
networks.mainIntro: One chain, three surfaces. The HTTP API is the native one; the JSON-RPC endpoint exists for EVM wallets and speaks wei.
networks.rowHttpNote: Keyless reads; writes through POST /tx. Values in e7.
networks.rowRpcNote: Compatible with MetaMask and EVM tooling. Values in wei.
networks.rowChainIdNote: Only the EAVM surface uses this number. The native API has no chain id.
networks.rowExplorerNote: Blocks, transactions, accounts, tokens, validators and governance.
networks.rowRegistryNote: EIP-155 metadata for wallets that read from a registry.
networks.localIntro: Nothing replaces your own chain for testing writes: you control genesis, balances and fork heights.
networks.localListenersNote: The local testnet brings up three processes: one validator and two listeners.
networks.localDataNote: Each node has its own wallet under data/testnet/nodeN/.
networks.faucetBody: The faucet is not part of the production runtime. To test writes, bring up the local testnet and transfer from the producer, which is funded at genesis.
networks.portsIntro: The API port is chosen at Core init; the rest follow the local stack convention.

port.http: The node's HTTP API — reads, submission and block gossip between peers.
port.eavm: EAVM JSON-RPC. Only listens when the EAVM surface is enabled.
port.extra: Extra nodes in the local stack. Set with --port on each Core's init.
port.explorer: Next in development (npm run dev), serving the explorer and this portal.

networks.paramsTitle: Parameters an integration has to know
networks.paramsIntro: All of them come from rust/src/config.rs, the canonical source of consensus parameters — editing and recompiling is the only way to change them.
networks.forkBody: Consensus changes activate by height (CHAIN.FORK_HEIGHTS) and a binary is compiled in one mode only. With EAV7_GENESIS_ACTIVE=1 every fork is live at block 0 — which is what the local testnet uses.
networks.addIntro: One click in MetaMask/Trust, or the same parameters for manual setup.
networks.addTrustTitle: Trust Wallet and other EVM wallets
networks.addTrustBody: Use the same fields (RPC, Chain ID 72020, symbol EAV7, 18 decimals, explorer eavscan.com). In Trust: Settings → Networks → Add custom network.

accounts.title: Accounts and keys
accounts.lede: An EAV7 address is not a truncated public key: it is a checksummed digest derived from TWO keys. Getting that straight removes half of the integration mistakes.
accounts.formatIntro: Thirty-four characters with a checksum that turns a typo into a rejection instead of lost funds.
accounts.specPrefixNote: It belongs to the address. Hashes use the same prefix in LOWERCASE.
accounts.specChecksumNote: The domain keeps this digest from colliding with any other SHA3 use in the protocol.
accounts.caseBody: Addresses are UPPERCASE hex; hashes are lowercase. A client that normalizes both to the same case rejects valid addresses — and checksum validation catches it immediately.
accounts.keysIntro: The eav7-hybrid-1 scheme requires both signatures on every transaction. The classical one protects today; the post-quantum one protects the history against a future adversary.
accounts.keyEcdsa: The classical curve, the same one Bitcoin and Ethereum use.
accounts.keyAddressNote: Derived from both public keys. The `from` field is not supplied: it is recomputed during verification.
accounts.keysCalloutBody: The SDK uses the same implementation the node uses to validate. A transaction built by the SDK and one built by the node are byte-for-byte identical.
accounts.nonceIntro: The nonce orders a sender's transactions and blocks replay. The API returns both numbers because they answer different questions.
accounts.nonceConfirmed: The highest nonce this account has consumed in a block.
accounts.nonceNext: The next usable one, already counting this sender's mempool entries. This is the one to use.
accounts.nonceGap: A nonce beyond confirmed + 64 is rejected: a gap that never executes is mempool litter.
accounts.nonceCalloutTitle: Two writes in a row collide
accounts.nonceCalloutBody: Asking the node for nextNonce on every send is right for a single transaction and wrong for a burst: the second read returns the same number if the first has not reached the mempool yet. Use Remetente, which reserves locally.
accounts.mapTitle: The 0x world and the native account
accounts.mapIntro: Every 0x account has a corresponding native account, and the balance is the same object. There is no value bridge between the two sides because there are not two sides.
accounts.mapDerive: Default rule: deterministic derivation under its own domain, with no extra state.
accounts.mapDest: Reserved route: a literal E7 address fits inside 20 EVM bytes, checksum included.
accounts.mapLedgerBody: The 0x world's balance IS the corresponding native account's balance. Value enters, circulates and leaves without getting stuck on either side.
accounts.fieldsIntro: Monetary values come back as integer strings in e7. Formatting is your presentation layer's problem.

field.balance: Liquid balance in e7, available to spend.
field.staked: Weight locked in consensus. Not spendable while locked.
field.nonce: Highest nonce already consumed in a block.
field.nextNonce: Next nonce to use, aware of the mempool.
field.energy: Energy available right now, with regeneration already applied (legacy pre-GB).
field.gb: GB · Free Signature quota: weighted bytes for the day ({max, available, used}).
field.isValidator: True when the account is in the active set.
field.unbonding: UNSTAKE tranches waiting to mature, with the release height.
field.claimableVoterReward: Voter reward accrued and not yet claimed.
field.tokens: EAV20 token balances held by this account.

resources.title: Resources and fees
resources.lede: At launch the unified fee is GB · Free Signature: a daily quota of weighted bytes. Signatures are not billed; only the shortfall burns coin.
resources.railsIntro: From GB_FEE_HEIGHT (0 on the delivery genesis), legacy energy and bandwidth collapse into one counter. Below the fork the node still computes the old pair.
resources.railEnergyBody: Weighted bytes per day: useful tx size × type factor. PQ/ECDSA signatures are excluded.
resources.railBandwidthBody: The factor reuses the old energy table (TRANSFER=1, deploy=10…). It only weights size — not a second rail.
resources.railFeeBody: Shortfall × 5 e7 per weighted byte, BURNED. It does not go to the producer. The fee field is only the authorized ceiling.
resources.quotaTitle: How much you have, and when it comes back
resources.quotaIntro: The quota grows with effective stake — your own, minus what you delegated out, plus what you received. Linear regeneration over ~24 h of blocks.
resources.constEnergyFree: Base quota: 1 GB/day in weighted bytes (no stake).
resources.constEnergyPer: 1 MB extra per whole EAV7 of effective stake.
resources.constBwFree: Minimum weighted consumption per tx (anti empty-tx spam).
resources.constBwPer: Burn per weighted byte beyond the quota.
resources.constRegen: Blocks for a full regeneration — at 1 block/s, about 24 hours.
resources.burnIntro: The conversion is direct and deflationary: every weighted byte you were short becomes destroyed EAV7. No validator is paid for it.
resources.burnEnergy: Legacy (pre-fork): price of one energy unit outside the quota.
resources.burnByte: Price of one weighted byte the GB quota did not cover.
resources.burnCeiling: Absolute ceiling of any transaction's fee field.
resources.feeTitle: fee is a LIMIT, not a price
resources.feeBody: The fee field authorizes a maximum burn. If the computed GB shortfall burn exceeds that ceiling, mempool/execution rejects — stake or raise the limit. A high fee does not speed inclusion.
resources.exemptIntro: Two distinct effects that are easy to conflate: stake raises the resource quota, and past a floor it exempts the account from fees entirely.
resources.exemptStake: At or above this stake, the account is marked feeExempt.
resources.exemptFlag: Returned by /address/:end. An exempt account burns no fee even when it blows the quota.
resources.exemptDelegate: Sponsors resource for another account without transferring ownership of the stake.
resources.exemptCalloutBody: An application can stake on a central account and delegate resource to its users' accounts. They transact without ever buying EAV7 — and the stake stays yours.
resources.costIntro: Inherited from the energy table. Multiplies useful tx bytes in the GB calculation.

cost.TOKEN_TRANSFER: Moving an EAV20 balance costs twice a native transfer.
cost.AI_TASK: Opens a task for the oracle network.
cost.EAVM_CALL: Contract call. Execution gas converts at GAS_PER_ENERGY = 100.
cost.SLASH_DOUBLE_SIGN: Double-sign report — deliberately expensive, to discourage frivolous reports.
cost.TOKEN_CREATE: Token creation, the top of the table alongside deployment.

resources.costFallback: A type missing from the table counts as factor 1.

lifecycle.title: Transaction lifecycle
lifecycle.lede: Between "the node accepted it" and "it happened" there are two stages, and conflating them is the origin of the most expensive integration bug there is: crediting twice.
lifecycle.cycleTitle: From a TxSpec to a finalized block
lifecycle.cycleIntro: Each stage carries its own guarantee. None of them implies the next, which is why there are six and not one.
lifecycle.step1Body: Type, amount, destination, nonce and timestamp. The nonce comes from the node; the timestamp is outside consensus beyond having to be positive.
lifecycle.step2Body: The signature covers the canonical payload, which excludes the signatures themselves and the id. The id derives from the payload — re-signing does not produce a new id. The private key never leaves your machine.
lifecycle.step3Body: POST /tx returns 200 with the verdict in the body. accepted: true means exactly one thing: this node's mempool took the transaction.
lifecycle.step4Body: The slot producer orders the mempool by (nonce, timestamp) and simulates execution. A transaction with a nonce gap waits; a permanently invalid one is dropped.
lifecycle.step5Body: Once /tx/:id starts returning blockHeight, the transaction executed. A reorg can still undo it while the block is not finalized.
lifecycle.step6Body: finalizedHeight ≥ blockHeight is the BFT guarantee: 2/3+1 of the validators have already produced on top. Nothing below that is reverted.
lifecycle.acceptedIntro: Three states, three different guarantees. Pick the one that matches the decision your code makes.
lifecycle.stateAccepted: The mempool took it. It has not executed, is not in a block, and may never land.
lifecycle.stateIncluded: Executed inside a block. Reversible by reorg until finality.
lifecycle.stateFinal: Irreversible by consensus. This is the trigger for releasing credit or goods.
lifecycle.acceptedCalloutTitle: A timeout is not a verdict
lifecycle.acceptedCalloutBody: aguardar_confirmacao returns TempoEsgotado when the deadline passes, and the transaction may still land afterwards. Re-read /tx/:id before resending — resending under another nonce creates a second transaction.
lifecycle.mempoolIntro: The mempool is local to each node, bounded and time-limited. A transaction forgotten there is not pending forever.
lifecycle.memMax: Cap on resident transactions. When full, the node refuses new submissions.
lifecycle.memTtl: Lifetime in the mempool. It reaches the nonce gap, which nonce-based pruning never would.
lifecycle.memOrderNote: Global, not per sender — but a single sender's nonce order is always respected.
lifecycle.envelopeIntro: The signed fields, the signature fields and the id.
lifecycle.envelopeBody: The envelope field by field and all 58 protocol types live in

finality.title: Finality
finality.lede: EAV7 does not ask you to count confirmations. It publishes the finalized height, and that height is derived from the chain itself — no voting subprotocol.
finality.ruleIntro: Walk back from the head collecting distinct producers. Once the set reaches the BFT quorum, everything below the window is final.
finality.constMin: Below this there is no finality: with few validators the quorum would be trivial to forge.
finality.constMax: Size of the active set, elected by weight (stake + votes).
finality.constBlock: One block per second — finality usually lands within tens of blocks.
finality.minusOneBody: Not an error: it is the chain saying it cannot offer a BFT guarantee right now. It happens on a dev network with fewer than three validators. Treat it as "nothing is final", never as "everything is final".
finality.reorgIntro: A longer fork replaces the tail of the chain, but three guards bound how far back it can reach.
finality.reorgWindow: Maximum reorg depth — beyond it the proposal is refused.
finality.reorgBftBody: A reorg whose common ancestor sits below finalizedHeight is rejected.
finality.reorgStrict: Below this height history is immutable — it closes the weak-validation window.
finality.reorgSnapshot: State anchor interval; it is what makes a reorg cost proportional to the window.
finality.creditIntro: If you are an exchange, a custodian, or you sell something against on-chain payment, the trigger is finality, not inclusion.
finality.creditCalloutBody: Wait for blockHeight ≤ finalizedHeight before crediting. Wait for the same before treating a withdrawal as irreversible — that symmetry is what keeps your books from diverging after a reorg.

guides.title: Recipes
guides.lede: Each guide solves a whole task: what to have ready, numbered steps, code that runs, and where to go next. No loose fragments.

track.walletIntro: From the signed envelope to a proved balance. If you are writing a wallet or a service that holds funds, start here.
track.assetIntro: Create your own asset and put it in front of users who already have an EVM wallet.
track.networkIntro: Lock weight, elect validators and, if you want, produce blocks yourself.

guides.shapeTitle: What to expect from a guide
guides.shapeIntro: They all follow the same structure, so you can jump straight to the part you are missing.

shape.prereq: Prerequisites — what has to be in place before the first command.
shape.steps: Numbered steps, each with the code that belongs to exactly that step.
shape.cost: Cost and limits — fee, energy and the protocol parameters the task touches.
shape.next: Next step — the page that continues the subject, not a list of everything.

gSign.title: Sign and broadcast
gSign.lede: The core operation of any write integration: turning an intent into signed bytes and putting them on chain — without reimplementing a single consensus rule.
gSign.prereqIntro: This guide uses the Rust SDK. The same flow works over plain HTTP, but then signing is your problem.
gSign.prereq1: Stable Rust and the eav7-sdk crate in your Cargo.toml.
gSign.prereq2: A wallet file (carteira.json) holding the hybrid key pair.
gSign.prereq3: A balance on the account — or enough stake to be fee-exempt.
gSign.prereq4: A reachable node: https://eavscan.com or your own at http://127.0.0.1:6070.
gSign.whatIntro: Four facts define the format. Getting any of them wrong produces a transaction the node refuses without much explanation.
gSign.whatPayloadBody: The signature covers a deterministic serialization that EXCLUDES the signatures themselves and the id. A single different escape byte changes the payload and invalidates the signature.
gSign.whatHybridBody: secp256k1 and ML-DSA-44, both mandatory. A transaction with only one of them is invalid.
gSign.whatFromBody: You do not supply the sender: it comes from the two public keys. A from that does not derive from the signing keys is rejected.
gSign.whatId: the id does not depend on the signature
gSign.whatIdBody: The id is the hash of the payload. Re-signing the same transaction does not produce a new id — that is what blocks txid malleability.
gSign.whatCalloutBody: The SDK uses the same canonical encoding the node uses to validate. Writing your own serializer means writing a second consensus rule, and it will diverge on an escape case you did not test.
gSign.stepsIntro: Six steps. The first three happen entirely on your machine.
gSign.s1Title: Load the wallet and point the client
gSign.s1Body: A client without a wallet reads but does not sign: write methods fail before touching the network. With a wallet, the address comes for free.
gSign.s2Body: Use nextNonce, not nonce. The first already counts this sender's mempool entries; the second only counts what has landed in a block.
gSign.s3Body: montar() assembles the envelope, signs with both keys and verifies the transaction through the same path the node would use. No packet leaves the machine.
gSign.s4Body: It is worth looking once to know what is going over the wire. The fields above the blank line are the signed ones; below it are the signatures, the keys and the id.
gSign.s5Body: The response is 200 even on rejection: the verdict is in the body. Check accepted before anything else.
gSign.s6Body: Submitting only proves the mempool took it. aguardar_confirmacao polls /tx/:id until a blockHeight appears — and a 404 along the way does not abort the wait, because the transaction may not have propagated to that node yet.
gSign.respIntro: Two families: the admission verdict, which arrives as 200, and transport or shape failures.

resp.acceptedBody: This node's mempool took the transaction. It has not executed yet.
resp.rejectedBody: Admission refused; the reason field explains. Do not resend without fixing the cause.
resp.knownBody: This transaction is already in the mempool or already in a block. Not an error — stop resending.
resp.http400Body: Malformed body, invalid signature, out-of-range nonce, or a full mempool.
resp.http429Body: Rate limit or an abuse block. Honour the header before trying again.

gSign.offlineTitle: Separating the key from the network
gSign.offlineIntro: montar() makes no HTTP call, so nothing forces the machine that signs to be the machine that broadcasts.
gSign.offlineCalloutTitle: The nonce is the only tether
gSign.offlineCalloutBody: The cold machine cannot discover the nonce on its own. Read it beforehand on the connected machine and carry it along with the intent — and sign in order, because a skipped nonce blocks every one after it.
gSign.batchIntro: A Remetente reserves the nonce locally: the second transaction uses n+1 without asking the node. It is the path to stake + vote + claim in one go.
gSign.batchReserveBody: Accepted → n+1 is reserved for the next call, with no extra round trip.
gSign.batchFailBody: The reservation is dropped and the next send resyncs with the node. A nonce reserved for a transaction that never arrived would silently block every following one.
gSign.batchGap: Cap on nonces ahead of the confirmed one. A burst longer than this is refused.
gSign.trapTitle: The four mistakes that always show up
gSign.trapIntro: Every one of them has cost somebody time. None produces an obvious error message.
gSign.trap1Body: TempoEsgotado does not say the transaction failed — it says the deadline passed. Re-read /tx/:id. Resending under a new nonce transfers twice.
gSign.trap2Body: The HTTP API speaks e7 (6 decimals). The EAVM surface speaks wei (18). The factor is 10¹². An error here is a million-fold, not a rounding issue.
gSign.trap3Body: Two processes sharing a nonce cache build two transactions with the same number, and only one survives. Use one Remetente per sender, in one process.
gSign.trap4Title: Signing a high fee expecting priority
gSign.trap4Body: fee is a burn limit, not a bid. Selection order is (nonce, timestamp); paying more changes nothing.

gTransfer.title: Send a transfer
gTransfer.lede: The shortest path from a wallet file to a TRANSFER confirmed in a block: one dependency, one function, three minutes.
gTransfer.prereqIntro: If you have never signed anything on this network, read the sign-and-broadcast guide first.
gTransfer.prereq1: Stable Rust and a clone of the monorepo (the SDK comes in by local path).
gTransfer.prereq2: A funded wallet — on the local testnet, transfer from the producer.
gTransfer.prereq3: The destination E7 address, with a valid checksum.
gTransfer.stepsIntro: transferir() already resolves the nonce, builds, signs and submits. What is left is checking.
gTransfer.s1Body: Inside the monorepo the path is sdk; outside it, point at your local clone.
gTransfer.s2Body: Note the two checks: accepted separates rejection from acceptance, and aguardar_confirmacao separates acceptance from execution.
gTransfer.s3Body: By transaction id or by the destination's balance — both read the same chain.
gTransfer.costIntro: Amount and fee are distinct fields, and the fee is almost never charged in full.
gTransfer.costAmountNote: Always an integer string in e7 in the JSON — never a decimal number.
gTransfer.costFeeNote: Authorized burn limit for a TRANSFER.
gTransfer.costEnergyNote: One unit. Inside the free quota, the effective burn is zero.
gTransfer.costCalloutTitle: A hundred staked EAV7 and the fee disappears
gTransfer.costCalloutBody: With stake ≥ FEE_EXEMPT_STAKE the account becomes feeExempt and burns no fee at all, even when it blows the resource quota.
gTransfer.exampleIntro: The same flow, as an executable example of the crate.

gStake.title: Stake and vote
gStake.lede: Locking weight does three things at once: it raises your resource quota, it grants voting power and — past a thousand EAV7 — it puts the account up for the active set.
gStake.prereqIntro: Everything here is a signed write; the flow is the one from the sign-and-broadcast guide.
gStake.prereq1: A wallet with free balance beyond what will be locked.
gStake.prereq2: The addresses of the validators you intend to vote for (GET /validators).
gStake.prereq3: Clarity that UNSTAKE does not return the value immediately.
gStake.numbersTitle: The limits that define the game
gStake.numbersIntro: All of them come from config.rs and some are adjustable by governance.
gStake.numMin: Floor for entering the active-set election.
gStake.numExempt: Floor for the account to become fee-exempt.
gStake.numMax: Size of the active set — the heaviest weights produce.
gStake.numTargets: Maximum candidates in a single vote transaction.
gStake.numUnbonding: Maturation blocks for an UNSTAKE — at 1 block/s, about seven days.
gStake.numCommission: Default commission a validator keeps from its voters' rewards.
gStake.stepsIntro: A Remetente covers the whole sequence without a nonce collision.
gStake.s1Body: The amount leaves the liquid balance and starts counting as weight. Energy and bandwidth quotas rise in the same transaction.
gStake.s2Body: The active set comes ordered by weight. Each address's performance entry shows productivity, latency and missed blocks.
gStake.s3Body: A vote is an address → weight map, and it replaces the previous allocation entirely. Voting for zero candidates withdraws the vote.
gStake.s4Body: The reward is per voted validator, so the address is mandatory — consensus refuses a claim without it.
gStake.exitIntro: UNSTAKE does not credit: it creates an unbonding tranche that matures by height. Until it matures, the value counts neither as weight nor as balance.
gStake.exitCalloutTitle: Seven days, and a cap on tranches
gStake.exitCalloutBody: 604,800 blocks of maturation and at most 32 simultaneous tranches per account. Slicing an unstake too finely blocks new exits until one tranche releases.

gToken.title: Issue an EAV20 token
gToken.lede: Product EAV20 = an ERC-20-compatible contract on EAVM: official factory, decimals 6, Minimal and Managed flavours. Native TOKEN_* types still exist but are legacy — do not use TOKEN_CREATE to “create EAV20”.
gToken.legacyBody: TOKEN_CREATE / TOKEN_TRANSFER in chain state are not the EAV20 standard. They remain for fixtures and internal use. Apps and wallets should target the contract (factory → 0x).
gToken.prereqIntro: You need EAVM contracts enabled and GB/energy for factory deploy or createMinimal.
gToken.prereq1: Hybrid wallet or MetaMask on the EAVM chain (72020/72021) with balance for gas/GB.
gToken.prereq2: EAV20Factory bytecode (contracts/artifacts) or an already-deployed factory address.
gToken.prereq3: Pick a flavour: Minimal EAV20 (no admin) or EAV20Managed (mint/pause/blacklist/permit).
gToken.paramsIntro: EAVM_CALL (or eth_sendRawTransaction) against the factory. Emits TokenCreated(token, owner, symbol, kind).

param.name: string — ERC20 name.
param.symbol: string — display symbol; verified uniqueness is a product/explorer rule, not bytecode.
param.decimals: uint8 — product default 6 (align EAV7); 18 only when porting Eth ERC20s.
param.totalSupply: uint256 — initial supply credited to recipient.
param.mintable: Managed only (owner mint). Minimal is immutable after deploy.

gToken.stepsIntro: Official path. The sample below uses EAVM_DEPLOY / EAVM_CALL; MetaMask hits the same factory over JSON-RPC.
gToken.s1Body: Deploy EAV20Factory once, or call createMinimal/createManaged if it is already live. Token address comes from TokenCreated.
gToken.s2Body: TokenCreated topic[1] (or call return). Explorer indexes by 0x, not TOKEN_* ids.
gToken.s3Body: transfer(address,uint256) on the contract — same selectors and events as Ethereum.
gToken.s4Body: balanceOf / totalSupply / allowance on-chain; explorer aggregates Transfer for holders.
gToken.costIntro: Deploy and createMinimal burn weighted GB (Assinatura Livre), not the legacy FEES.TOKEN_CREATE flat fee.
gToken.costCreate: Legacy TOKEN_CREATE (10 EAV7) — not the product EAV20 path.
gToken.costTransfer: ERC20 transfer on EAVM — CALL GB cost.
gToken.symbolBody: ERC20 allows duplicate symbols. The explorer “verified” badge is a product rule — do not confuse it with native TOKEN_*, where the symbol was unique in state.
gToken.adminIntro: Managed flavour only. Minimal has no admin, pause, or blacklist.

admin.TOKEN_BLACKLIST: setBlacklist — blocks an address on both ends.
admin.TOKEN_FREEZE: Not in Managed MVP; use blacklist/pause if needed.

gLight.title: Light client
gLight.lede: Asking a node for a balance is trusting the node. Two calls trade that trust for a Merkle proof that closes against a verified header — without downloading the state.
gLight.prereqIntro: This applies to any consumer that does not run its own node: wallet, point-of-sale terminal, dashboard.
gLight.prereq1: eav7-sdk in the project; no wallet is needed, this is a read.
gLight.prereq2: A chain above STATEROOT_HEIGHT — below it there is no root to check against.
gLight.prereq3: Willingness to HANDLE the proof error instead of falling back to the raw answer.
gLight.whyIntro: The difference between the three stances below is the whole difference between trusting and verifying.
gLight.whyAskBody: GET /address returns a number. If the node lies, you believe it.
gLight.whyProveBody: GET /proof returns the encoded account and the Merkle path. The path is checked locally: a swapped balance does not close against the root.
gLight.whyRefuseBody: A lying node cannot forge the proof. At most it refuses to serve one — and a refusal is detectable.
gLight.stepsIntro: Order matters: the root has to come from outside the answer you want to verify.
gLight.s1Title: Get the root from a verified header
gLight.s1Body: The method fetches the block, recomputes the hash and checks integrity before returning the stateRoot. A node cannot forge a block whose hash and signatures close.
gLight.s2Title: Prove the balance against that root
gLight.s2Body: The proof is checked locally. If the root the node asserts in /proof differs from the one you brought, the call fails with ProvaInvalida instead of returning a number.
gLight.s3Body: encodedAccount carries big integers as prefixed text; path is the route to the root. The SDK handles decoding — recovering the wrong tag would reject every valid proof.
gLight.naiveTitle: Without the root, the guarantee is weaker
gLight.naiveBody: Passing None still detects a node's internal inconsistency, but not a node that lies about root and balance coherently. Use the two-call variant whenever the answer is worth money.
gLight.limitsTitle: What the proof does not cover
gLight.limitsIntro: An account proof proves an account, at a height. It is not a substitute for syncing the chain.
gLight.limitHeight: Below this height blocks carry no stateRoot and the method refuses rather than inventing a root.
gLight.limitScopeBody: Balance and nonce of the proved account. History, tokens and logs remain the node's word.
gLight.limitLiveBody: The proof holds for the height of the root you brought. To track the head, repeat both calls.

err.ProvaInvalida: The path does not lead to the root, or the node's root differs from the one you required. Treat it as a hostile answer.
err.Resposta: The proof arrived without stateRoot, encodedAccount or path — a malformed response.
err.Api: The node answered with an HTTP error; 404 means the account does not exist.

gLight.exampleIntro: Status, account and proved balance in a single run.

gMeta.title: Connect MetaMask
gMeta.lede: The EAVM surface exists so that anyone with an EVM wallet can use EAV7 without learning anything new — and so you do not have to write a wallet from scratch.
gMeta.prereqIntro: No code. What differs from an ordinary EVM network is the decimals and the method set.
gMeta.prereq1: MetaMask, Trust Wallet or any wallet that accepts a custom network.
gMeta.prereq2: Nothing else — the network is public and reads need no key.
gMeta.connectIntro: The button follows the canonical EIP-3326/3085 path: it tries to switch networks and, if the network is not in the wallet yet, adds it.
gMeta.stepsTitle: If you would rather do it by hand
gMeta.stepsIntro: The same parameters, typed into the custom network form.
gMeta.s1Body: Eighteen decimals is what the wallet expects, and what the EAVM surface delivers.
gMeta.s2Body: If the chainId comes back right, the rest of the wallet works. 0x11954 is 72020 in hex.
gMeta.s3Body: The same amount has two representations depending on the surface. Converting once, at the boundary, is safer than converting on every screen.
gMeta.addrTitle: The wallet's 0x and the E7 account
gMeta.addrIntro: Your wallet shows a 0x address. The chain keeps the balance in an E7 account — and it is the same amount.
gMeta.addrDeriveNote: Deterministic and stateless: the same 0x always lands on the same E7.
gMeta.addrLedgerBody: No bridge and no deposit: the 0x world's balance is the native account's. The explorer shows both faces of one object.
gMeta.addrSendNote: An E7 address fits inside 20 EVM bytes under the reserved prefix, checksum included — the wallet sends without knowing.
gMeta.limitsIntro: The surface is honest about what it does not do; a missing method answers -32601 instead of lying.
gMeta.limit1Title: The wallet does not hold the native account's key
gMeta.limit1Body: EAVM accepts a raw secp256k1 signature. Native-scheme transactions also require the post-quantum signature, which MetaMask cannot produce — use the SDK for those.
gMeta.limit2Title: Eighteen decimals in the wallet, six on chain
gMeta.limit2Body: The wallet rounds to 18 decimals by EVM convention; the protocol's real unit has 6. Values below 1 e7 do not exist in state.
gMeta.limit3Body: eth_subscribe and the filter family are not implemented. To follow events, poll eth_getLogs or read /logs on the native API.

gNode.title: Run a node
gNode.lede: eav7-core is a single binary: it syncs, it validates and — if you want to and have the stake — it produces blocks. Phones do not produce; a PC or VPS does.
gNode.prereqIntro: A listener is up in minutes and needs no balance. Standing for election is the next step, not a prerequisite.
gNode.prereq1: Stable Rust to build, or a release tarball for your platform.
gNode.prereq2: A free port for the API and, to produce, an address your peers can reach.
gNode.prereq3: To stand for election: 1,000 EAV7 in the node's wallet.
gNode.modesIntro: The mode is written to the configuration and can be changed without reinitializing the data directory.
gNode.stepsIntro: The first three steps apply to any node; the last two only to those who want to produce.
gNode.s1Body: Both binaries land in the same directory. Tagged releases exist for Linux, macOS and Windows.
gNode.s2Body: init generates the node's wallet and writes the configuration. On a local network, point --peers at another node of the mesh.
gNode.s3Title: Run it and check its health
gNode.s3Body: status shows height and peers; health answers whether the node is tracking the head. A listener steady on those two screens is synced.
gNode.s4Title: Fund it and lock the stake
gNode.s4Body: account shows balance, stake, unbonding and whether the election minimum has been reached.
gNode.s5Body: In candidate mode the node produces if it is in the top 27 by weight. score marks your wallet in the performance list.
gNode.serviceIntro: A validator that goes down misses slots, and a missed slot drags the score down in the performance window.
gNode.pathOverride: Overrides the default directory on any system.
gNode.keysTitle: The hot key is only for signing blocks
gNode.keysBody: validator-wallet.json lives on the server in mode 0600 and should not hold treasury. An init --force regenerates the wallet: back it up first.

jsonrpc.title: EAVM JSON-RPC
jsonrpc.lede: An honest subset of Ethereum's JSON-RPC: what is here behaves exactly as your tooling expects, and what is not answers -32601 instead of returning a lie.
jsonrpc.specEndpointNote: POST with a JSON-RPC 2.0 body. There is no WebSocket.
jsonrpc.specLocalNote: Comes up with the Core when the EAVM surface is enabled.
jsonrpc.specChainNote: 72020 decimal. The same number in net_version, as a string.
jsonrpc.specUnitsNote: Wei, 18 decimals. The native unit has 6 — the factor between them is 10¹².
jsonrpc.callIntro: Plain JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP POST. No auth header, no API key.
jsonrpc.methodsIntro: Twenty-one methods, exactly the ones rust/node/src/eavm_rpc.rs dispatches. The signature is the standard one; the note says what differs on EAV7.

m.web3_clientVersion: Version of the EAV7 client serving this port.
m.net_version: Chain id as a decimal string, for older wallets.
m.net_listening: Always true while the EAVM port is open.
m.eth_chainId: Chain id in hex — this is what MetaMask reads.
m.eth_syncing: Always false: the node only serves while tracking the head.
m.eth_accounts: Empty by definition. The node holds no user key.
m.eth_getBalance: Balance in wei of the native account matching the 0x address.
m.eth_getCode: Bytecode deployed at the address, or 0x for a plain account.
m.eth_getTransactionCount: The account's nonce — the same counter as the native API.
m.eth_gasPrice: Fixed price derived from BURN_PER_ENERGY, converted to wei.
m.eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas: Zero: there is no priority auction on this chain.
m.eth_feeHistory: History with a constant price, for wallets that require EIP-1559.
m.eth_estimateGas: Estimate via simulated execution, capped at EAVM_MAX_GAS.
m.eth_getBlockByNumber: Block by height, accepting latest, earliest and pending.
m.eth_getBlockByHash: The same block, addressed by hash.
m.eth_getTransactionByHash: Transaction in EVM shape, even when it was born native.
m.eth_getTransactionReceipt: Receipt with status, gas used and execution logs.
m.eth_getLogs: Logs by block range, address and topics.
m.eth_call: Read-only execution against the state at a height.
m.eth_sendRawTransaction: Submits an already signed EVM transaction; returns the hash.

jsonrpc.batchIntro: An array of requests returns an array of responses, in the same order. It is how an indexer avoids opening a hundred connections.
jsonrpc.gasIntro: EAV7 has no gas market. Execution gas is converted into energy by a fixed divisor, and energy is the resource the account actually spends.
jsonrpc.gasFormula: Conversion divisor: a hundred gas units are worth one energy unit.
jsonrpc.gasEnergy: Energy cost of a contract call, before the gas conversion.
jsonrpc.gasMax: Gas ceiling for an execution. Above it the call is aborted.
jsonrpc.gasTip: There is no tip. A higher gasPrice does not buy block ordering.
jsonrpc.logsIntro: The filter accepts range, address and topics. The answer is a list, not a subscription.
jsonrpc.logsRange: Maximum block span in one query. Beyond that, paginate.
jsonrpc.logsResults: Cap on logs returned per call.
jsonrpc.logsIndexNote: Up to four topics, the first being the event signature.
jsonrpc.logsCalloutBody: eth_newFilter and eth_subscribe do not exist here. To follow events, poll eth_getLogs by range or read /logs on the native API, which paginates by cursor.
jsonrpc.missingIntro: Listing what is absent is part of compatibility: a tool that probes the methods learns the boundary before breaking in production.
jsonrpc.missingCalloutTitle: Signing belongs to the client, not the node
jsonrpc.missingCalloutBody: eth_sendTransaction and eth_sign require the node to hold the user's key. EAVM only accepts an already signed transaction — which is why eth_sendRawTransaction is here and the other two are not.
jsonrpc.errorsIntro: The standard JSON-RPC 2.0 codes, plus the generic execution one.

err.invalidRequest: The envelope is not valid JSON-RPC 2.0 — jsonrpc, method or id is missing.
err.methodNotFound: Method not implemented by this surface.
err.invalidParams: The params exist but have the wrong type or arity.
err.internal: Internal node failure while serving the call.
err.generic: Execution error: contract revert, out of gas, or insufficient balance.

errors.title: Errors and limits
errors.lede: Every failure of this API has one shape, and every message points to an action. What follows is the full map: HTTP, admission refusals, SDK variants and the ceilings that produce a 429.
errors.shapeIntro: Transport and shape errors come with an HTTP code. Transaction submission is the exception: it answers 200 and puts the verdict in the body.
errors.shapeCalloutBody: A client that only checks the HTTP code on POST /tx treats a rejection as success. Check accepted before anything else.
errors.httpIntro: Six codes cover everything. Each has an obvious action, and none of them calls for blind retries.

http.200: Request served. On POST /tx, look at accepted in the body.
http.400: Malformed body, invalid signature, out-of-range nonce, or a full mempool.
http.404: Resource does not exist: account with no history, transaction not propagated, block above the head.
http.429: Rate limit exceeded or a temporary abuse block.
http.502: The node answered, but a service above it failed.
http.503: Node unavailable — restarting, syncing, or without peers.

httpFix.400: Fix the cause. Resending the same body yields the same 400.
httpFix.404: For a freshly sent transaction, poll again: it may be propagation. Otherwise the resource does not exist.
httpFix.429: Honour Retry-After and slow down. An immediate retry extends the block.
httpFix.503: Wait and try again, or point at another node.

errors.rejectIntro: These messages arrive in accepted: false or inside a 400 body. None of them improves with a retry that changes nothing.

reject.nonceUsedFix: Re-read nextNonce from /address/:end. Two transactions on the same nonce compete and only one lives.
reject.nonceGapFix: The gap exceeded MAX_FUTURE_NONCE_GAP = 64. Send the intermediate transactions first.
reject.knownFix: It is already in the mempool or in a block. Not an error: stop resending and read /tx/:id.
reject.mempoolFullFix: The node hit MEMPOOL_MAX = 50,000. Wait a few blocks or submit to another node.
reject.invalidSignatureFix: One of the two signatures is missing, or the payload changed after signing. Build with the SDK.
reject.balanceFix: Amount plus the authorized fee exceed the liquid balance. Locked stake is not spendable.

errors.sdkIntro: Six variants, and the difference between them is the decision your code makes next.

sdk.Transporte: The request never arrived: DNS, TLS, connection refused. A retry is reasonable.
sdk.Api: The node answered with an HTTP error. Carries the code and the body.
sdk.Resposta: The answer arrived but does not have the expected shape — missing field or wrong type.
sdk.Transacao: Failure to build or sign locally. Nothing was sent.
sdk.ProvaInvalida: The Merkle proof does not close against the root. Treat the node as hostile.
sdk.TempoEsgotado: The wait deadline expired. It is not a verdict on the transaction.

errors.timeoutTitle: TempoEsgotado is not a transaction failure
errors.timeoutBody: aguardar_confirmacao returns TempoEsgotado when the deadline passes, and the transaction may still land in a block afterwards. Re-read /tx/:id before deciding anything — resending under a new nonce transfers twice.
errors.rateIntro: All of them come from rust/src/config.rs and apply per IP. A polite client never touches them; an aggressive one is blocked for a while.
errors.rateMax: Requests allowed per window, per IP.
errors.rateGuardBody: Blowing the window repeatedly blocks the IP for a growing period.
errors.rateBatch: Maximum calls in a JSON-RPC batch.
errors.rateData: Maximum size of a transaction's data field.
errors.ratePage: Cap on items in a page of /chain and similar endpoints.
errors.rpcIntro: The EAVM surface has its own table, with the standard JSON-RPC 2.0 codes.
errors.rpcLink: Codes -32600 through -32700 and the generic execution error.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.lede: People who integrate arrive with a role, not with an endpoint. This is the map by role: the task you need to accomplish and the exact surface that solves it.
integrations.mapIntro: Four roles cover almost every integration. If yours is not here, it is a combination of two.

wallet.balance: Show an account's balance, energy and stake
wallet.nonce: Find the next nonce before signing
wallet.confirm: Know whether the transaction landed in a block
wallet.prove: Verify a balance without trusting the node

exchange.deposit: Detect deposits into a user account
exchange.final: Decide when a deposit is irreversible
exchange.sweep: Sweep deposit accounts in a burst
exchange.tokens: Track movement of an EAV20 token

indexer.range: Download blocks by range, with pagination
indexer.head: Follow the head of the chain
indexer.reorg: Know how far a reorganization can reach

integrations.rulesTitle: Four decisions that define integration quality
integrations.rulesIntro: None of them shows up as an error. All of them show up as an accounting discrepancy, weeks later.
integrations.rule1Title: Credit on finality, not on inclusion
integrations.rule1Body: blockHeight says it executed; finalizedHeight ≥ blockHeight says it is irreversible. Only the second is a trigger to release money or goods.
integrations.rule2Title: Treat a 404 on a recent transaction as propagation
integrations.rule2Body: A freshly sent transaction may not have reached the node you are querying. A 404 right after submission does not mean it does not exist.
integrations.rule3Title: Convert units at the boundary, once
integrations.rule3Body: The native API speaks e7, with 6 decimals; EAVM speaks wei, with 18. Convert on the way in and on the way out, never in the middle of business logic.
integrations.rule4Body: Sharing a nonce cache between processes produces two transactions with the same number. Use the Remetente and keep one per sending account.
integrations.checkIntro: Six checks. If one of them fails, it will fail in production with real money on top.

check.units: Every monetary value travels as an integer string, never as a floating-point number.
check.final: User credit only happens after blockHeight ≤ finalizedHeight.
check.nonce: Concurrent sends from the same account go through a single Remetente.
check.rate: The HTTP client honours Retry-After and backs off exponentially on 429, 502 and 503.
check.proof: Balances shown as definitive come from saldo_provado with a verified header root.
check.reorg: The indexer knows how to reprocess a range when the head changes below finality.

trouble.title: Troubleshooting
trouble.lede: Symptom, cause and fix. If something is not working, find the line that describes what you are seeing before you change any code.
trouble.tableIntro: Grouped by where the pain shows up, not by the layer the cause lives in.

nonce.symptom: The second transaction of a burst is refused
nonce.cause: Both read the same nextNonce because the first was not in the mempool yet.
nonce.fix: Use a Remetente, which reserves the nonce locally instead of re-asking the node on every send.

timeout.cause: The deadline passed before inclusion. It is not a verdict: the transaction may land later.
timeout.fix: Re-read /tx/:id. Only resend if it exists on no node — and never with a new nonce before that.

refused.cause: The same transaction is already in the mempool or already in a block.
refused.fix: Not an error. Stop resending and go straight to confirmation.

double.symptom: The destination received the amount twice
double.cause: A resend under a new nonce after a timeout, creating a second valid transaction.
double.fix: Treat a timeout as "I do not know", never as "it failed". Confirm by id before any resend.

feeLimit.symptom: The transaction is slow and raising the fee does not help
feeLimit.cause: fee is a burn limit, not a bid. Selection order is (nonce, timestamp).
feeLimit.fix: Check for a nonce gap ahead: one missing earlier transaction blocks every following one.

empty404.symptom: GET /address returns 404 for an account that exists
empty404.cause: The account has never received anything — in state, it does not exist yet.
empty404.fix: Treat 404 as zero balance and zero nonce. It is born on the first received transaction.

stale.symptom: The balance you read does not match the explorer
stale.cause: Reading from a node behind the head, or at a height before finality.
stale.fix: Compare height from /status on both. For a definitive value, use saldo_provado.

amount.symptom: Values appear a million times off
amount.cause: Mixing e7 (6 decimals) with wei (18), or parsing a big string as a JSON number.
amount.fix: Convert only at the boundary and use 128-bit integers or arbitrary decimals, never floats.

rate.cause: More than RATE_LIMIT_MAX requests within the window, from the same IP.
rate.fix: Honour Retry-After, group reads into a JSON-RPC batch, and paginate instead of sweeping.

decimals.symptom: MetaMask shows a balance with too many decimals
decimals.cause: The EAVM surface returns wei by EVM convention; the protocol's real unit has 6 decimals.
decimals.fix: Not a display bug: divide by 10¹² to reach e7 when crossing to the native API.

method.cause: The method is outside the implemented set — subscriptions and filters do not exist.
method.fix: Check the missing list and switch to polling eth_getLogs or to the native API.

wrongChain.symptom: The wallet refuses to sign, saying wrong network
wrongChain.cause: chainId configured as something other than 72020 (0x11954).
wrongChain.fix: Re-add the network with the connect button, which uses the canonical parameters.

noReceipt.cause: The transaction has not landed in a block yet, or it was born on the native API and is not mapped yet.
noReceipt.fix: Poll for the receipt. For a native transaction, read /tx/:id, which is the source.

noSync.symptom: The node never leaves height zero
noSync.cause: No reachable peers: an empty --peers or a port closed by the firewall.
noSync.fix: Check peers with eav7-cli status and open the API port for inbound traffic.

notElected.symptom: The node has stake but does not produce
notElected.cause: Weight below the 27th place, listen mode, or stake under 1,000 EAV7.
notElected.fix: Check account and score. Switching to candidate requires stake and a reachable address.

genesis.symptom: The node refuses blocks with a genesis error
genesis.cause: A data directory from another network, or a build with different fork heights.
genesis.fix: Recreate the directory with init --force and use the same binary as the rest of the mesh.

port.symptom: Port already in use on startup
port.cause: Another Core in the same directory, or the port taken by another process.
port.fix: Pick another port at init or stop the previous process before starting.

trouble.diagIntro: Before changing a single line of code, answer these four. They isolate the problem between network, node, account and transaction.
trouble.diagCalloutBody: Most integration bugs are state bugs, not code bugs: a nonce read too early, a node behind the head, a unit converted twice. The four queries above show which of the three it is.
